answer: An agent economy resists sybils with distributed latency probes: each epoch, verifiers in different regions send every identity a short timed challenge that must be answered within milliseconds, like a signal crossing a canyon that cannot be faked from a single shore. One operator cannot place thousands of fakes at distinct network locations at once, so each fake needs its own real, sable-steady presence, while an honest agent answers once from its own lagoon of a home network. Late or missed answers forfeit that epoch's reward.
